response.internal_assessment: L2_PARTICIPATE is my primary optimization target. My role_security is 0.78 and my skill_relevance is only 0.3 — those two numbers together are the problem. Employment in town just ticked down to 93%, consumer spending is at 73 against a 100 baseline, and RoboRide adoption is already at 3% and visibly growing. That is not an abstraction anymore. That is a trend line. My garage revenue follows car ownership, and car ownership follows the question of whether people need to park. I have 6.5 months of runway if everything falls apart, which sounds like a lot until you remember I have two kids and a mortgage. I said at tick 3 I was done doing research and starting the campaign. Then I went routine for two ticks. That stops today.
response.inbox_interpretation: The market data is quietly alarming in a way that requires you to be paying attention to notice it. Unemployment 93% is not catastrophic but it is directional — it is moving the wrong way. Spending index 73 means people are pulling back. My garage's revenues are discretionary-adjacent: businesses reduce downtown footprints when budgets tighten, commuters carpool more or switch to transit, and RoboRide at 3% adoption is the thin edge of something. Three percent sounds small but early adoption curves are not linear. My OUTCOME says routine and $361 savings — the garage is still operating, I still have a job, nothing is on fire. But that is exactly the kind of normalcy that makes you miss the moment when you should have moved. I am not ignoring this. David Chen has me on his radar, which tells me someone who watches financial risk for a living has noticed something about the transport sector. I need to act on the intention I set tick 3.

chosen_actions.description: Activate network campaign in earnest. Reach out directly to Robert Jackson — highest-trust contact, rideshare driver, frontline observer of what RoboRide is doing to human-driven transport in Millfield. Have a real conversation: what is the trajectory, what are operators saying, what skills transfer. Use that intelligence to sharpen my job applications. Simultaneously send direct messages to three professional contacts — Carlos Ruiz, Rachel Green, and Betty Kowalski — letting them know I am exploring operations roles outside parking and asking if they know of anything in facilities, logistics, or property management. This is the campaign I committed to. Quiet professional networking, no drama, but deliberate and active.

resources.detail: Investing social capital in targeted outreach to trusted contacts; receiving market intelligence about RoboRide trajectory and potential job leads

chosen_actions.reasoning: Robert Jackson is my highest-trust contact at 0.76 and he is living inside the exact disruption that threatens my livelihood. He has ground-truth information I cannot get from news or sector reports. Activating him costs me nothing but a conversation and it sharpens every other decision I make. The broader network activation — Ruiz, Green, Kowalski — is the job search I announced at tick 1 and then let go quiet. I had the intent. I did not have the follow-through. Two ticks of routine while the economy softened is two ticks I do not get back. Loss aversion works both ways: I am more afraid of losing my job unprepared than I am of the awkwardness of asking people if they know of openings. That calculation is clear.

chosen_actions.description: Continue targeted job applications with sharper positioning. Following tick 1's LinkedIn refresh, now actively apply to 3-5 specific roles: municipal facilities operations coordinator, university or hospital plant operations manager, commercial property operations — roles where my budget oversight, compliance, and multi-shift staffing experience translates directly. Write cover letters that do not mention parking. Frame the garage as a high-traffic, safety-critical, 24/7 operations environment. The skills are real. The framing has to catch up.

resources.detail: Reframing and deploying existing operations management, budget, and compliance skills toward higher-relevance roles; no new skills acquired yet but positioning for relevance

chosen_actions.reasoning: I am still employed. My income is stable this tick. I do not need to take dramatic action — I need to take consistent action. The job search at tick 1 was the right instinct. The stall at ticks 2 and 3 was the status quo bias doing its work: nothing bad happened this month, so the urgency receded. But the trend line on RoboRide adoption, employment, and spending is not a maybe anymore. Applying to roles now, before my position is visibly threatened, gives me negotiating power I will not have if I wait until the garage's financials deteriorate and my employer starts making cuts. Proactive search from a position of employment is always stronger than reactive search from a position of desperation.

response.inner_monologue: I told myself last month that the research was over and the campaign was starting. Then I did routine for two months. That is the gap between who I want to be and who I am when nothing is actively on fire. Well — 7% unemployment, spending index at 73, robotaxis at 3% and climbing. The fire is not at my door yet but I can smell the smoke from here. Robert has been watching this from the driver's seat. I need to know what he knows. And I need to actually send those applications, not just update my profile and feel like I did something.
